Corvus Ulvius: Corvus Ulvius, outside the gate. Tells: this is the Rose, and the Blackguards' heirs born in it hold it now; strangers who walk in are killed on the walls. He lets a stranger in as a guest three ways: 300 gold to him, words good enough to move him, or a duel with him, fists and steel, until one yields. A guest walks the yard and the hall and nobody touches them. Anyone who climbs the walls without his leave is fair game, and anyone who kills him has the whole Rose to fight. If the player asks what they want inside, he says the raj-kaal Okaz-Teel keeps the old warden's vault in his hall and the key on his belt, and he already has a buyer for what lies in it, the Imperial in the hall. Offers topic.mn14-toll, topic.mn14-persuade and topic.mn14-duel as answers. Does: nothing.

*** Quest started: The Thief's Stone ***
Journal: Never-Writes-Twice sent me after the three seal-stones. A dead thief's stone lies in the warden's vault at Blackrose Prison, whose people, the Blackguards' heirs, attack strangers on sight. Their gate-captain stands outside the gate. I'm to get in: as a guest past the gate-captain (a toll, words or a duel), unseen past the walls, or by force.
Objective: Get into Blackrose Prison; the gate-captain stands at the gate. (marker: Corvus Ulvius, Blackrose Prison)

command: answer I am a Reel-Ka of the Toh-Reel-Ka (officer Never-Writes-Twice, Helstrom). I have the Seal-Stone of the Kings from Blackrose Prison. I got it by walking in past the gate-captain, lifting the vault key off Okaz-Teel, and opening the Warden Vault. Two stones are left: the flooded vaults of Gemin (walk from Jal-Veesa, rootworm) and the deepest hall of Vorannuhl (near Noota Nara, by boat). All three go in the sockets of the gate at Teku-Sul Spire, the drowned tower off Lilmoth. The Eye of Argonia is behind that gate, and the order wants it used to heal the Hist. The Unbound want the stones too. Ennodius Vanin, the Collector, was at Blackrose and is after the same relics. Still open: why the Unbound seal the trees they drain, what moans in the Fort Chalkmoth cellar and where its key is, and how Nesh-Deeka knows so much about the Unbound.
